classification.difficultyReason: Apply the explicitly requested sine rule to opposite pairs in obtuse triangles. The harder part first requires calculating the missing angle using the triangle angle sum.

content.prompt: Use the sine rule to find the value of $x$, correct to two decimal places.

spec.description: Narrow oblique triangle. External leader identifies the upper-left angle; ordinary source blue strokes use house black.
spec.mathematics: Upper-left angle 10 degrees; middle-right angle 140 degrees; opposite sides respectively 12 cm and x cm.

spec.description: Triangle with vertical right side and external leader to the top angle. Ordinary outlines and labels use house black.
spec.mathematics: Top angle 18 degrees; lower-left angle 95 degrees; vertical side opposite 95 degrees is 7 m; side joining lower-left to top is x m.

answer.worked:
The third angle is $180^\circ-95^\circ-18^\circ=67^\circ$.

By the sine rule,
$$\begin{align*}\frac{x}{\sin67^\circ}&=\frac{7}{\sin95^\circ}\\x&=\frac{7\sin67^\circ}{\sin95^\circ}\\x&\approx6.47\text{ m}.\end{align*}$$
